say.text: Last stretch: a cold check. No hints and no retries, so answer as you would in the exam.
How ready do you feel?

choices.label: Ready, straight to the cold check
Shaky, give me a quick refresher

say.text: Level sets the picture: vomiting is early in a high block, while distension and late constipation mark a low one.
Strangulation overrides the wait: constant pain, tachycardia and a raised lactate mean surgical review now.
Tempting: adhesions are the textbook commonest cause in adults, so that answer comes first.
Wrong for this setting: that is the current-practice answer. The Indian PYQ key expects hernia. Right: hernia is the PYQ key; adhesions is current practice.

sure_note.text: You were sure: the exam key and current practice differ here, so hold both.

say.text: Yes. The PYQ key for India and developing countries is hernia, and an irreducible groin lump points there first.
A district hospital in India. An adult has had three days of intestinal obstruction, with a tender, irreducible lump in the groin.
Which cause do you name as the most common here?
Tempting: adhesions are the commonest adult cause, so the default answer arrives first.
Wrong here: the history line rules them out, because adhesions need a previous operation. Right: in a virgin abdomen, check the orifices, then look for a tumour.

sure_note.text: You were sure, and the history line decides it: no surgery means no adhesions.

say.text: Yes. With no previous surgery and no hernia, a tumour is the next cause to find.
An adult has small bowel obstruction and has never had abdominal surgery. The groin and other hernial orifices were examined and are normal.
What is the likeliest cause?

choices.label: Adhesive bands, the commonest adult cause
A tumour blocking the bowel lumen

say.text: Tempting: diverticular disease is common in older adults and often narrows the colon.
Wrong: common is not commonest. Right: colorectal carcinoma is the commonest adult cause, and the left colon is where it blocks.
Yes. Colorectal carcinoma is the commonest adult cause of large bowel obstruction.
A 68-year-old man has large bowel obstruction. He has had six weeks of constipation and a six-kilogram weight loss, and no previous surgery.
What is the commonest cause in adults?

choices.label: Diverticular disease, the commonest adult colon cause

say.text: Yes. The distal bowel empties first in a large bowel block, so constipation comes early and vomiting late.
Tempting: vomiting is the first sign of obstruction, so it feels like the first sign at every level.
Wrong: vomiting is early only in a high small bowel block. Right: a low block distends and constipates early, and vomits late.

sure_note.text: You were sure, and vomiting is early only in a high block.

say.text: A 70-year-old man has had no flatus for two days. His abdomen is markedly distended, and he vomited once, late in the course.
Which timeline fits a large bowel block?
Tempting: a post-operative belly is distended, and paralytic ileus is the familiar label.
Wrong: in paralytic ileus the abdomen is silent. Right: tinkling means active peristalsis pushing against a block.

sure_note.text: You were sure, but loud tinkling shows working peristalsis, not a failed gut.

say.text: Yes. In mechanical obstruction the gut works hard against the block, so sounds are hyperactive and tinkling.
A patient three days after surgery has distension and vomiting. The nurse hears loud, high-pitched tinkling every few seconds.
What does this suggest?

choices.label: Paralytic ileus: loud sounds mean the gut has stopped
Mechanical obstruction: peristalsis pushing against a block

say.text: Tempting: colicky pain is the classic symptom of obstruction, so the label sticks.
Wrong: the word constant and the pulse change the picture. Right: constant pain with tachycardia and localised tenderness means strangulation until proved otherwise.

sure_note.text: You were sure, and constant pain with a fast pulse is the strangulation pattern.

say.text: Yes. Constant pain, tachycardia and localised tenderness suggest strangulation, not simple obstruction.
A man with known adhesive obstruction, on day two, says his pain was colicky but is now constant and severe. His pulse is 124 and one area of the abdomen is tender.
How do you read this?

choices.label: Simple obstruction; colicky pain is still the picture
Strangulation until proved otherwise; urgent surgical review

say.text: Tempting: indirect inguinal hernia is the commonest groin hernia, so it feels the riskiest.
Wrong: frequency is not risk. Right: the femoral neck strangulates, and femoral is the groin hernia most likely to strangulate.

sure_note.text: You were sure: commonest and most dangerous are different questions.

say.text: Yes. A femoral hernia has a narrow, rigid neck, and a partial-wall strangulation can give few obstruction signs.
Tempting: strangulation feels like complete obstruction, with vomiting and distension.
Wrong: Richter's traps only part of the wall, so it can strangulate with few obstruction signs. Right: a rising lactate, not the vomit, shows the strangulation.

sure_note.text: You were sure, but a partial-wall strangulation can be quiet on the obstruction signs.

say.text: A thin, multiparous woman has a tender, irreducible swelling below the inguinal ligament. She passes flatus, has no vomiting, and her lactate is rising.
Which diagnosis fits best?

choices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia, the commonest groin type
Femoral hernia, strangulated, with few obstruction signs
Richter's hernia, so vomiting and distension should be complete

say.text: Yes. In adults the intussusception usually has a lead point, often a tumour, so resection is needed.
Tempting: intussusception is classically reduced by enema, and the diagnosis is familiar.
Wrong: age changes the cause. Right: a child's intussusception is usually idiopathic, but an adult's is usually driven by a lead point, so resect.

sure_note.text: You were sure, and the adult lead point is the reason to resect.

say.text: A 45-year-old man has intermittent colicky pain and a palpable mass. CT shows an intussusception.
What is the management?

choices.label: Air enema reduction, as for a child

say.text: Tempting: surgery feels safest in a child with obstruction, so theatre seems the default.
Wrong: a stable child without peritonitis gets a reduction under imaging. Right: peritonitis, perforation, shock or failed enema reduction send the child to surgery.
Yes. Peritonitis, perforation, shock or failed enema reduction are the indications for surgery in a child.
A two-year-old has an intussusception on ultrasound. The child has been resuscitated and is stable.
Which finding sends this child to theatre rather than to an enema?

choices.label: Any intussusception in a child, since surgery is safest

say.text: Yes. Gangrene, perforation or failed detorsion call for emergency resection, usually Hartmann's.
Tempting: detorsion is the usual first step for sigmoid volvulus, so it feels like the whole treatment.
Wrong: a gangrenous loop should not be detorted and left in the abdomen. Right: assess the bowel; gangrene means emergency resection.

sure_note.text: You were sure, but detorsion is for a viable loop, and this one is gangrenous.

say.text: An elderly man has a sigmoid volvulus with peritonitis. The bowel looks gangrenous at the start of the operation.
What is the right operation?

choices.label: Endoscopic detorsion, then elective colectomy later

say.text: Tempting: a stent avoids a large operation, and it is a real option on the left.
Wrong: a stent is a bridge or palliation on the left, not the standard for a right-sided tumour. Right: the right colon is resected.

sure_note.text: You were sure, and a stent is not the right-sided standard.

say.text: Yes. Obstructing right-sided cancer is treated by right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis.
A stable, fit patient has an obstructing carcinoma of the ascending colon.
Which is the standard definitive treatment?

choices.label: Self-expanding metallic stent, the standard for right-sided tumours

say.text: Tempting: a plain film already confirms obstruction, so it feels complete.
Wrong: the X-ray is the initial test, and it answers whether there is obstruction, not why. Right: CT answers the why and where.
Yes. The X-ray is the initial test; contrast-enhanced CT is the investigation of choice for the cause and level.
Tempting: barium is the traditional test in many textbooks.
Wrong: a barium meal is a slow study that does not stand in for CT. Right: contrast-enhanced CT is the definitive test for small bowel obstruction.
An adult has small bowel obstruction. A plain abdominal X-ray shows dilated loops.
Which test best shows the cause and the level?

choices.label: Repeat erect and supine X-ray; the first film is definitive
Barium meal follow-through as the definitive test

say.text: Tempting: the bird's beak and the claw are both enema signs, so they blur together.
Wrong: the bird's beak is a volvulus sign on contrast enema. Right: the claw is the intussusception sign on enema.
Yes. A bird's beak on contrast enema is a volvulus sign; the coffee bean on plain film is the sigmoid one.
A contrast enema of an elderly constipated patient shows a 'bird's beak' at the end of a loop of bowel.
Which condition does this sign belong to?

choices.label: Ileocolic intussusception: the bird's beak is its enema sign

say.text: Tempting: both markers are folds, so they feel interchangeable.
Wrong: haustra are the large bowel's markers and do not cross the full width. Right: folds that cross the lumen mark the small bowel.
Yes. Valvulae conniventes cross the full width in the small bowel, and loops lie centrally.
A supine film shows central loops with folds crossing the full width of the bowel, like a stack of coins.
Which bowel, and which marker?
Yes. The 3-6-9 rule gives small bowel 3 cm, colon 6 cm and caecum 9 cm, widening distally.
Tempting: six is the middle number of the rule, so it feels as if it fits any bowel.
Wrong: the six belongs to the colon. Right: small bowel 3, colon 6, caecum 9.
Tempting: three looks like the small digit, so it feels right for the widest segment.
Wrong: the caecum is the widest segment at 9 cm. Right: 3 is the small bowel.
A plain film is read against the upper normal diameters of the 3-6-9 rule.
Which pairing of segment and upper normal diameter is correct?
Tempting: a gallstone is sorted by where it impacts, and the impaction feels like a wall problem.
Wrong: the question is whether the cause lies inside the lumen, in the wall, or outside. Right: the stone sits in the lumen.
Yes. A gallstone sits in the lumen, so it is intraluminal. Its standard emergency operation is enterolithotomy.
Tempting: the stone came from the gallbladder, which is outside the bowel.
Wrong: the fistula is the route in, but the stone lies in the lumen. Right: intraluminal, treated by enterolithotomy.
A gallstone passes through a fistula and blocks the bowel. This is gallstone ileus.
Into which class of obstruction does it fall, by its relation to the bowel wall?

choices.label: Intramural, since it impacts in the bowel wall
Intraluminal, since it sits inside the bowel lumen
Extramural, since it presses in from outside

say.text: Yes. Contrast reaching the colon within 24 hours predicts resolution without surgery.
Tempting: 72 hours is the number you remember from the trial, so it feels like the check time.
Wrong: 72 hours is the limit of the conservative trial, not the contrast check. Right: 24 hours for contrast, 24 to 48 for a second look, 72 as the limit.

sure_note.text: You were sure, and 72 hours is the limit, not the check.

say.text: An adult with adhesive small bowel obstruction is treated without surgery. A water-soluble contrast study is done.
Which timing predicts that the obstruction resolves without surgery?

choices.label: Contrast in the colon within 24 hours
Contrast in the colon at 72 hours

say.text: Tempting: the operation feels decisive, so it seems the first act.
Wrong: fluids, potassium and decompression come first. Right: resuscitate and decompress, then decide.

sure_note.text: You were sure, but the operation is not the first step in a dehydrated patient.

say.text: Yes. Resuscitate and decompress, check the hernial orifices, then a non-operative trial with its 24-hour contrast check.
Tempting: the 72-hour rule is famous, so the trial feels safe to start.
Wrong: the trial comes after a hernia or closed loop is screened out. Right: examine the orifices first, then the trial with its 24 and 72 hour limits.

sure_note.text: You were sure, but a hernia must be excluded before any trial.

say.text: An adult has adhesive obstruction. There is no peritonitis on examination, and the patient is dehydrated and vomiting. The hernial orifices have not been examined yet.
What comes first?

choices.label: Emergency laparotomy first; fluids and the tube can follow
Resuscitate, check orifices, then a 24-hour-checked trial
Start the 72-hour trial now; the orifices can wait

say.text: Your take-home: the level of block sets the picture, strangulation overrides the wait, and drip and suck come before any decision.
Your review cards follow, and each one returns on a spaced schedule.

cards.q: Which cause is the PYQ key for intestinal obstruction in India and developing countries?
cards.a: Obstructed or strangulated hernia. Current practice names adhesions as the commonest adult small bowel cause.

cards.q: In which block does constipation come early?
cards.a: A large bowel block: the distal bowel empties first, so absolute constipation is early and vomiting late.

cards.q: Which change in pain and pulse suggests strangulation?
cards.a: Colicky pain becoming constant and severe, with tachycardia and localised tenderness.

cards.q: Which bowel shows valvulae conniventes crossing the full width?
cards.a: The small bowel. Haustra mark the large bowel and do not cross the lumen.

cards.q: Investigation of choice for small bowel obstruction in an adult?
cards.a: Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen. The plain X-ray is the initial test.

cards.q: What does a coffee bean on plain film mean?
cards.a: Sigmoid volvulus. A bird's beak on contrast enema is also a volvulus sign.

cards.q: What does contrast in the colon within 24 hours predict in adhesive obstruction?
cards.a: Resolution without surgery. 72 hours is the limit of the trial.

cards.q: Which groin hernia is most likely to strangulate?
cards.a: Femoral, because its neck is narrow and rigid.
Resect, since a lead point is usual. A child gets an enema unless there is peritonitis or another criterion.

cards.q: Standard emergency treatment for gallstone ileus?
cards.a: Enterolithotomy, removing the stone through a proximal longitudinal enterotomy.
